dhashHamming.note: 64-bit dHash. Deltas are uniformly 28-38 with no spike, which is the signature of one continuous take at steady speed — there are no hard cuts.

reference.camera_notes: One unbroken 37-second take — no cuts, no dissolves, no speed ramps. The camera is a virtual pedestrian: eye height reads as roughly 1.5-1.6 m (the horizon consistently sits at monitor-top / desk-return height, with the ceiling grid fully visible above and floor material readable below), and it never tilts — pitch stays locked at 0, so verticals remain vertical for the whole take. Motion is a slow forward dolly at roughly 0.6-1.0 m/s, well under real walking pace, with a smooth ease-in at the head and no hand-held shake or head bob whatsoever; the impression is a gimbal on a slider rather than a person. Yaw is a continuous, unhurried right-hand turn of about 4-6 deg/s that accumulates to roughly a half-turn across the take: it opens in the reception lounge looking square at the fluted timber reception desk, arcs right past the glazed conference room, and closes deep in the open-plan floor facing the opposite window wall. The path deliberately threads at least three thresholds so the plan reads as connected space rather than a set of stills: the glass-partition edge sweeps the frame at about t=8, a freestanding portal frame passes at close range at about t=16, and a further glazed room line passes at about t=28. Each threshold pass momentarily fills a third of the frame with a near-field element, which is what sells depth. Composition keeps one strong near-field anchor on the left or right edge (millwork, a planter, a desk return) while the vanishing point sits slightly off-centre down the circulation spine. Lighting is a warm interior key around 3000K from downlights and linear pendants, balanced against bright daylight through full-height perimeter glazing; the exterior is deliberately blown out one to two stops so foliage and city read as luminous backdrop rather than detail. Shadows are soft and ambient-occlusion-driven, there are no hard sun patches on the floor, and there is a mild bloom on the window plane. Mean frame luminance holds in a very tight 0.61-0.67 band across all ten samples, i.e. the exposure never swings. Branding is IN-SCENE ONLY: the qbiq roundel plus wordmark appears on wall-mounted displays at roughly t=8.3, t=12.4 and t=16.5. There is NO title card, NO end card, NO lower-third and NO watermark anywhere in the take.

branding.description: qbiq roundel + wordmark rendered as content on wall-mounted displays.

target.$comment: What gate G7 asserts about out/walkthrough.mp4. Deliberately a superset of the reference: we add a branded title card because the deliverable pack is sent to a client cold, whereas qbiq's video ships inside their own web UI.
target._pHashRationale: Reference first/mid/last pairs measure 33-38. A threshold of 12 passes any genuinely moving camera while failing a frozen or duplicated frame.
target._luminanceRationale: Reference frames sit at 0.61-0.67 with sd 0.21-0.27. The gate band is widened so a darker scheme still passes; the floor and the stdDev check are what reject black / blown / flat-empty frames.

branding._note: DEVIATION FROM REFERENCE: qbiq ships no title card (branding is in-scene only). The mission brief requires 'logo detectable on the title card frame', so DSource adds one. Set branding.mode to 'in_scene' here to match qbiq exactly and G7 will skip the title-card assertion instead of failing.

camera.note: Reproduce the reference's single continuous take. Do NOT add cuts, shake, or pitch.
